title: Prototyping a new racing game idea and I need honest feedback
author: jaykrown
selftext:
Ground mode, ZERO friction, thrust vectoring only. Drift mode vibes (not shown was the ability to down thrust).

Flight mode, proper aerodynamics flight model. 

Few I will note, the texture of asphalt/concrete is weird if there's no friction, probably ice or smooth metal would be better looking, will update easily. Edges clipping into ground should be fixable.

Am I wasting my time with this idea, or does the video interest you? Any issues? What would you want to see, what seems strange? Unoriginal and already done? Suggestions about modeling, what visual style you'd like to see? 

Let me know, I seriously appreciate any comments, even if a bit harsh, let it rip. Thank you!

comments.author: grafixcoder
comments.body:
This looks really cool.

From a personal standpoint, I've always found the floaty/vector thrust controlled vehicles really difficult and frustrating to control (think back to even asteroids).  It's not the most intuitive controls (at least for me) and takes a lot of practice to master.

Looking at the video though, it looks like you have the start of something that could be an awesome battle type of shuffleboard/curling game mechanic though.  Vector thrusting combined with some sort of explosive behavior could make for a very fun mechanic that takes the real-time steering part out of the equation.

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body: Thanks, what do you think would be a battle mechanic that would fit well? That's an interesting perspective, I appreciate it.

replies.author: grafixcoder
replies.body: I think it would be some sort of throw/spin, then a limited amount of thrust to influence the "puck" with some sort of detonation mechanic.  It takes the steering part out of the slide mechanic which is the part that tends to be difficult to control with low friction and a thrust mechanic.

comments.author: TropicalAviator
comments.body: Would play it tbh, super cool

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body: Thanks! And if you ever have any suggestions, please let me know. I'm going to push for another increment into this pre-alpha before deciding whether I want to get it to the beta state or not. Your feedback seriously helps. For the next version I'll try to get it hosted on a web page free access so you can actually try it out for yourself.

comments.author: Initii
comments.body: So, its basically Didikong racing? Or Sonic Transformers?

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body: Thanks for mentioning those, I looked at some gameplay for both. Neither seem to have actual aerodynamics? It seems like in each zone in those games is what dictates what vehicle you use.

comments.author: blacklabel251
comments.body: Based on this video the controls look clumsy but that may be the point. My biggest piece of feedback tho is that currently it feels way too slow. You say things like "zero friction" "drift" "down thrust" and I think SPEED. I would try playing with your overall speed and game feel elements like camera warp and parallax effects.

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body: Thanks I'll make the thrust stronger so you have more control over your direction allowing for faster acceleration and higher speeds, hopefully that helps.

replies.author: blacklabel251
replies.body: You should also check out a game called Exos One. It’s not quite the same thing but has a nice ground to air mechanic that feels great when you get in the groove.

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body: Indeed I've seen it, the mechanic where you plummet downwards and slide to gain momentum is really interesting because it turns your downward force into horizontal speed.

comments.author: japherwocky
comments.body:
The ground based driving looks incredibly clunky, and the flying looks really fun.  I was totally uninterested until you took off, and then I thought, "well shit why ever stop flying?"  

I'd step into the physics a little more if you're going to do the ground thing, maybe not totally zero friction

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body: It is pretty clunky, I think the map could be a lot smoother with higher walls, letting you "surf" up and use your momentum. Currently I was trying to do more traditional style having to change my trajectory by burning backwards which is janky. I'll lean into the idea of like half pipe "pump" style where your down thrust could help propel you because there's no friction. Thanks for commenting.

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body: The flying was the hardest part, but once I got the feel for it then it worked out. Problem is the control scheme, has to change when you transfer between ground and flying, which is something that takes time to get used to. I imagine with a gamepad it may be easier than keyboard.

comments.author: TopTippityTop
comments.body:
1. Imo it looks a bit frustrating to drive, needs a stronger sense of control
2. The flight mode could be gliding mode only, so if you gain speed first you have more control options/longer runway. That adds more skill and forethought into the drive

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body: Great feedback I appreciate it. I mentioned in another response I think that making thrust stronger will help give more control and power, also map design making walls higher so you can really slide up and use them to your advantage like a half pipe. The flight mode already causes aerodynamic drag, so overall you float slower than sliding.

comments.author: IMJorose
comments.body:
The idea looks awesome, but the execution needs a couple of passes, I think. As others already pointed out, the level of control is too low at the moment.

I would totally play a more mature version.

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body: Thank you, I think making control more powerful will help the most easily. The thrust in hindsight does feel quite under powered. Another thing will be the map design, walls should be higher so you can really drift up them and carry momentum back down. I'll be updating it over the next week, and aim to have the next version playable in browser for free to test. I appreciate your feedback, and if you think of anything else please feel free to let me know.

comments.author: Grimnoc
comments.body:
In addition to what everyone else said here about having more control, camera, and speed, it needs to have THE most important thing: fun factor.

How do you think you can improve the replayability for your target audience? Currently, if you have like 10 different maps, I can see the players going through only two of them before they say, "Okay, I've seen all there is to this". There is no current draw to keep players engaged.

Sure there is the element of competitiveness in racing games, but that's only going to get you so far, especially as an indie game where you don't have the backing of a franchise to use as a crutch for lack of game mechanics.

Find something fun/unique to add and build upon that. You've got to make it standout.

Oh and if you got to this point in the post and decided that your game definitely meets the the fun and/or unique criteria of what I'm talking about and that "you're good," I'm also here to tell you that you are "not good". You need more, especially with the rise of the hobbyist game devs so has recently enabled. I'm not trying to sound harsh or rude. I'm just trying to be objective to help your project grow. Good luck! I believe in you.

comments.author: RemarkableWish2508
comments.body:
I'm going to say no.

Turning around, or heavily to one side, just to slow down and/or change direction feels awfully clunky. Particularly when you need to face forward and get aerodynamic drag while flying. Makes flying look like a much more controllable experience.

You could probably make it more "fun" and "playable" by cheating and simply multiplying the thrust vector by a factor of the radians relative to the movement vector, so something like "visual 30° right" would have the effect of a "90° right", while a "90° right" could have the effect of "2x 180° back".

I'd try some different values to see which one feels more playable.
